note: Adapted for publication from a rubric pre-registered on 2026-10-28, before any R1 submission. Removed for privacy: a fifth dimension about the original user's own career capital, the user's four candidate topics (T1-T4) and the pairwise picks involving them, and a weight set built for the user. The two remaining weight sets were renormalized over the four public dimensions. Nothing was added.

options.D01: Pre-training and foundation models: scaling, architecture, data, training dynamics; foundation-model training in academia
options.D02: Post-training, RL and reasoning: RLVR, reward models, test-time compute
options.D03: Agent learning, continual learning and self-improvement: long-horizon credit assignment, memory, experience replay, recursive self-improvement (by layer)
options.D04: Agent systems and ecosystem: environments and benchmarks, tool use, computer use, harnesses, open-source agents
options.D05: Evaluation science: evaluating LLMs, agents, multimodal models and robots; LLM/VLM-as-judge; statistical rigor; when an evaluator can be trusted
options.D06: Embodied AI and robot learning: VLAs and robot foundation models, generalization, reliability, failure recovery, learning in deployment, touch
options.D07: Generative policies and world action models: diffusion/flow policies, video as policy, models that predict observations and actions together
options.D08: World models and spatial intelligence: interactive video generation, 3D/4D representations, action-conditioned latent dynamics, JEPA-style representation prediction
options.D09: Simulation and synthetic data: physics simulation, generative simulation, sim2real, digital twins, synthetic training and evaluation data
options.D10: Autonomous driving: end-to-end planning, closed-loop evaluation and simulation, long tail and safety, fleet data engines
options.D11: Multimodal understanding: MLLM/VLM architectures, visual grounding, spatial and video understanding, multimodal reasoning
options.D12: Multimodal generation: diffusion/flow foundations, few-step generation, unified understanding and generation, video and 3D generation, evaluating generation
options.D13: Interpretability, alignment and safety: mechanistic interpretability, scalable oversight, robustness, monitoring
options.D14: AI infrastructure and algorithm-system co-design (short): long context and KV cache, low precision, MoE, RL rollout systems, inference-compute allocation

dimensions.impact: If it works within ten years, how much it changes AI capability or the industry
dimensions.bottleneck: Whether it is the bottleneck or lever that decides progress (without it, other progress stalls) rather than a nice-to-have
dimensions.academic_edge: Whether academia, including academic labs with GPUs, can make a contribution industry can't make and that then gets adopted; not whether it can publish
dimensions.window: Timing: whether a newcomer can still own a piece of it now; low if already absorbed, commoditized or overcrowded

overall: The persona's own overall score, weighted by the persona's own values; not the average of dimensions. In the original run it also weighed the removed user-specific dimension, so it is shown as recorded and marked as such in the report.

levers.L1: Evaluation and verification (benchmarks, evaluators, statistical rigor, trustworthiness)
levers.L2: RL and post-training (RLVR, rewards, online learning)
levers.L3: Simulation and synthetic data (physics simulation, generative simulation, sim2real)
levers.L4: World models and world action models (models that predict future observations and actions)
levers.L5: Scale and quality of real data (robot data, human video, deployment data)
levers.L6: Architectures and new paradigms (non-LLM routes, representation learning)
levers.L7: Scaled-up foundation models (bigger pre-training, more compute)
levers.L8: Systems and efficiency (infrastructure, inference, training efficiency)

lever_allocation: Split 100 points across L1-L8: over the next 5-10 years, which levers most decide progress in AI (physical AI and agents especially) and most deserve a researcher's bet.

named_questions.Q1: Levers: which kind of lever most decides AI progress over the next 5-10 years? Is evaluation really the safest bet, or RL, simulation, world models or world action models?
named_questions.Q2: Academic foundation models: academic labs with GPUs can train foundation models (open VLAs, video or world models, open LLMs). For a student at the undergraduate-to-master's stage, is joining this kind of work the highest-impact path?
named_questions.Q5: Late entry: for each direction, which way of taking part is already too late, and why (absorbed, automated or commoditized)?
named_questions.Q6: Taste: if you could give someone starting out in AI research one piece of advice on research taste, what would it be, and which of your experiences makes you say it?

Q2.question: Under which conditions would you say yes to Q2?

conditions.C1: A narrow-domain model (VLA, video or world model and similar), not general LLM pre-training
conditions.C2: Credible third-party evaluation already exists for that domain
conditions.C3: A team of 2-4 people with complementary skills, not one person alone
conditions.C4: Lab compute at scale (for example 64 H100-class GPUs usable continuously for months)
conditions.C5: Open weights with a path to outside adoption

aggregation.primary: Per option: median, IQR, min, max of persona `overall`. Sort by median; ties go to the smaller IQR.
aggregation.sensitivity: Flag options whose rank moves 3+ places across weight sets.
aggregation.baselines: Two no-persona baselines, reported separately; never pooled into the medians.
aggregation.movement: Per persona and option, the R1-to-R3 change in overall; every change cites a post.
aggregation.empty_concession: An argument marked accepted or partly accepted in the debate whose option score does not move in R3 is logged as an empty concession.
